# BigQuery

<!-- BEGIN generated by .github/scripts/plugin_pages.py from the package's describe.json -->

Google BigQuery: the `bigquery` source, from the `bigquery` package. Declare the package once in `dependencies.yml`; DRE installs it on demand:

```yaml
# dependencies.yml
plugins:
  - bigquery
```

### Profile fields

Set in `profiles.yml`, under `connections:`, in a target with `type: bigquery`.

| Field | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `method` | `oauth` | How to sign in: oauth (gcloud application-default credentials), service-account (a key file), service-account-json, oauth-secrets or external-oauth-wif. |
| `project` |  | The Google Cloud project to read from (dbt's `database` also works); required, checked by the plugin. |
| `dataset` |  | Default dataset for unqualified table names (dbt's `schema` also works) |
| `location` |  | Where jobs run, e.g. US, EU or europe-west2. |
| `keyfile` |  | Path to a service account key file, for method service-account. A file path; `~/` is your home directory. |
| `keyfile_json` |  | A service account key's JSON, inline, for method service-account-json. Secret: use `env_var()`. |
| `token` |  | An OAuth access token, for method oauth-secrets. Secret: use `env_var()`. |
| `refresh_token` |  | An OAuth refresh token, for method oauth-secrets with client_id and client_secret. Secret: use `env_var()`. |
| `client_id` |  | OAuth client ID, for method oauth-secrets with a refresh token. |
| `client_secret` |  | OAuth client secret, for method oauth-secrets with a refresh token. Secret: use `env_var()`. |
| `token_uri` |  | Where a refresh token is exchanged (default https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token) |
| `workload_pool_provider_path` |  | The workload identity pool provider, for method external-oauth-wif. |
| `token_endpoint` |  | Where the external identity's token comes from, for method external-oauth-wif: type, request_url, request_data. |
| `service_account_impersonation_url` |  | The service account to impersonate after workload identity federation. |
| `impersonate_service_account` |  | A service account email to run as, using the signed-in identity. |
| `scopes` |  | OAuth scopes (default: bigquery, cloud-platform and drive) |
| `execution_project` |  | The project jobs run and are billed in, when not `project` |
| `quota_project` |  | The project API quota is charged to. |
| `priority` |  | Interactive (default) or batch. One of `interactive`, `batch`. |
| `maximum_bytes_billed` |  | A job that would bill more bytes than this fails instead of running. |
| `job_execution_timeout_seconds` |  | Stop a query that runs longer than this. |
| `job_creation_timeout_seconds` |  | Give up starting a query after this long. |
| `retries` | `3` | How many times to try starting the session again after a temporary error (0: never) |
| `job_retries` |  | How many times a query that fails with a transient error is run again (default 1) |
| `job_retry_deadline_seconds` |  | Stop retrying a query after this long. |
| `api_endpoint` |  | A BigQuery API endpoint other than Google's, e.g. Private Service Connect or an emulator. |

<!-- END generated -->

## Notes

An alpha: `bigquery` is published as 1.0.0 pre-releases (`1.0.0-alpha.N`), which `dre deps`
installs while there's no stable release. It is tested against the BigQuery emulator; sessions,
`load` and dry runs need the real service. Field names and values are dbt-bigquery's, so a dbt
profile can be copied across; dbt fields that only matter for building models (`threads`,
Dataproc, `gcs_bucket`, ...) are accepted and ignored.

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `method` | `oauth` (default: gcloud's application-default credentials, from `gcloud auth application-default login`), `service-account`, `service-account-json`, `oauth-secrets` or `external-oauth-wif`. |
| `project` | Required. The project tables are read from. dbt's `database` works too. |
| `dataset` | Default dataset for unqualified table names. dbt's `schema` works too. |
| `location` | Where jobs run, e.g. `US`, `EU`, `europe-west2`. |
| `keyfile` | For `service-account`: path to a key file. |
| `keyfile_json` | For `service-account-json`: the key's JSON, as a YAML map or a string. |
| `token` | For `oauth-secrets`: an access token. |
| `refresh_token`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `token_uri` | For `oauth-secrets`: a refresh token and its OAuth client. |
| `workload_pool_provider_path`, `token_endpoint`, `service_account_impersonation_url` | For `external-oauth-wif` (Microsoft Entra): `token_endpoint` has `type: entra`, `request_url` and `request_data`. |
| `impersonate_service_account` | Run as this service account, using the signed-in identity. |
| `scopes` | OAuth scopes. Default: BigQuery, Cloud Platform and Drive (for Sheets-backed tables). |
| `execution_project` | The project jobs run and are billed in, when not `project`. |
| `quota_project` | The project API quota is charged to. |
| `priority` | `interactive` (default) or `batch`. |
| `maximum_bytes_billed` | A job that would bill more fails instead of running. Set on every job. |
| `job_execution_timeout_seconds`, `job_creation_timeout_seconds` | Stop a query that runs, or takes to start, longer than this. |
| `retries` | How many times to try starting the session again after a server error, a rate limit or a dropped connection (default 3). |
| `job_retries`, `job_retry_deadline_seconds` | A query that fails with a server error or rate limit runs again, up to `job_retries` times (default 1) within the deadline. |
| `api_endpoint` | A BigQuery API endpoint other than Google's (Private Service Connect, an emulator). Results are then read over REST only. |

```yaml
connections:
  bq:
    targets:
      dev:        # you, through gcloud
        type: bigquery
        project: my-project
        dataset: reporting
        location: EU
        maximum_bytes_billed: 10000000000
      prod:       # a service account, for the scheduler
        type: bigquery
        method: service-account
        keyfile: /secrets/reporting-sa.json
        project: my-project
        dataset: reporting
        location: EU
```

Capabilities: `sessions`, `check`, `load`. `open` starts a BigQuery session and every job of the
Binding runs in it, so temp tables last for the whole Binding. `check` is a dry run: BigQuery
validates the statement, and the bytes it would process are logged (`-v` shows them).
`load` creates a temp table in the session from one SQL statement, with a warning.

Results come through the Storage Read API (Arrow) when the client library uses it, which it does
for results larger than one page, and over the REST API otherwise or when the identity can't
create read sessions (`bigquery.readsessions.create`). Both give the same output.

The package is written in Go, on Google's official BigQuery client. DRE stores nothing for
BigQuery: sign-in goes through Google's own libraries.

## Test the billing and data projects separately

The dev profile above is a minimal application-credential connection with a billing cap.
Use the [tutorial](../examples/tutorial/) structure with `bigquery` declared and a result
query `select 1 as connection_check`. Run `dre validate --live <report>` before previewing.
For business data, adapt the [monthly finance workbook](../examples/monthly-finance/) to
BigQuery tables and dialect; replace any DuckDB-specific SQL.

Use `execution_project` when jobs should run in a different project from the data, and
`quota_project` for API quota attribution. `priority: batch` suits scheduled work that can wait;
`interactive` suits immediate previews. `maximum_bytes_billed` rejects an unexpectedly large
scan rather than merely warning.

`connection-failed` can mean missing application credentials on the runner. `query-failed`
can mean dataset location mismatch, data access denied, or a query beyond the billing cap.
Choose the dataset's `location`, grant data and job permissions to the actual runner identity,
and narrow the SQL before raising a cap. See [profiles](reference-profiles.md),
[error codes](reference-error-codes.md) and [connection](glossary.md#connection).
